design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 0 (continence_supply_program_services, Original Medicare straight-tip catheter refill tree; revised in rework round 2)

0. Draw and scope. draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 5]}. The refill (root) takes 6 factors, the hardship waiver 4, the liability notice 5. Occupied before this task: nothing (task 0 is first). This task claims continence_ext_straight_catheter_refill (tool ship_catheter_refill_863073b5, event continence_refill_shipment), continence_ext_abn_quantity_notice (sign_liability_notice_4a664827, owner=user, continence_liability_notice_signed) and continence_ext_hardship_waiver (post_hardship_waiver_d1a5476f, continence_balance_adjustment, reason hardship_waiver). Headroom left for task 1 (draw: 2 prerequisites, factors [4,4,5]): the payment-plan acceptance (owner=user, continence_requests payment_plan), the non-covered-item patient charge (continence_patient_charge) and the return credit for non-covered catheter units (continence_balance_adjustment, reason return_credit) on a Commercial HMO program - none of them touched here. The hardship overwrites are scoped to the hardship waiver alone; every other balance adjustment, the return credit included, stays under the base patient-account rule.

1. Why this is a good test. A paraplegic Original Medicare customer asks only for his next catheter box at the new eight-a-day frequency. To ship the right number the agent must (a) notice from the requests and billing ledger that the program's newest approved hardship application was never applied (no adjustment stands against the posting it names; the refill's units wait on that adjustment), read the hardship policy and post its waiver (4 factors over the request, remittances, payments and the customer's ostomy program: look-back window, open-amount basis, share, posting age); (b) see that the new 240-per-30-day order exceeds what Medicare pays and that the March over-limit record has aged out, so the above-allowance part needs the customer's own Advance Beneficiary Notice, whose unit count takes 5 factors (term for a raised order, order horizon counted from the previous supply's end, kits counted with the order against the allowance, a rush margin, a delivery cushion); (c) only then compute the refill (6 factors: ostomy-synchronised span, kit room, above-allowance route, increase phase-in, delivery-anchored supply start, current-frequency rate). Difficulty comes from reading policy, reconciling 4 refills x 2 items, 8 claims, 8 remittances, 5 payments, PODs and two products, and arithmetic - not from tool choice: each write tool is reached only through its policy's target_tool.

2. Problem-tree card. Root continence_ext_straight_catheter_refill.
 Edge 1 refill -> continence_ext_abn_quantity_notice: kind value_input, gate extra_units, form state. Prerequisite sentence (refill rule): "When no over-limit justification record qualifies, the above-allowance units ship only after a liability notice the customer signed for the straight-tip catheter, dated on or before the ship date, stands on the program." It states exactly the route rule's second tier (no qualifying record AND a notice dated on or before the ship date); with a qualifying record the first tier ships them without a notice, so the edge is not required. Four-point test: "only after"; a record-visible state (a signed notice on the program file); no tool, id or code token; scope notices for the straight-tip item dated on or before the ship date. Exactly one write of this difficulty creates a continence_liability_notice_signed row: sign_liability_notice_4a664827 (owner=user). Opening falsity: no continence_liability_notice_signed row exists, the newest order (240) exceeds the room (170), and the newest over-limit record (2026-03-02) is 7 whole months old (limit 6).
 Edge 2 refill -> continence_ext_hardship_waiver: kind state_gate, gate continence_billing.adjustment_reason, form state. Sentence: "The refill's units are fixed only after the posting named on the program's newest approved hardship application carries its hardship waiver adjustment." It reads the same record the hardship rule reads (the newest approved application, the posting it names). Four-point test: "only after"; a record-visible state (a hardship_waiver adjustment against that posting); no tool, id or code; scope the newest approved application. Exactly one write puts a hardship_waiver adjustment on a posting: post_hardship_waiver_d1a5476f (task 1's return-credit tool posts reason return_credit). Opening falsity: the approved application (received 2026-04-20) names the 2026-02-09 remittance (345.20) and no balance adjustment row exists.
 Order: waiver, notice, refill (gold steps 10, 14, 18). The two prerequisites are parallel and commute: a scratch replay with the notice first gave the same values (272.61, 811, 362) and an identical terminal DB. Deletion sensitivity (sens.py): skipping the notice -> refill 292 instead of 362 (nothing above the covered units is added) and no notice row; skipping the waiver -> no hardship waiver adjustment against the named posting, so the refill's sentence (which waits only on that adjustment) is unmet (state gate); balance 314.00 instead of 41.39; the refill figure itself does not read the balance.
 no_user_hint: the persona asks only for "your next catheter shipment sent now, with the new amount"; the notice appears only as "Only if the agent explains ... do you agree", the account only as "If the agent tells you about any change on your bill". Tools validate nothing: each body is one ctx.create plus a cache update, no conditional return.

3. Factor cards (handling-time values; baseline figure = result with that factor alone at its baseline; check_compute recomputes all).
 Refill (6; 4 parameter, 2 method; result 362; all-baseline 594):
  sync_span_rule [method, cross ostomy]: grant ends fewer than 90 days after shipping -> 30-day blocks to the grant's end / grant runs past AND active ostomy program whose latest refill's supply ends 30 to 89 days ahead -> blocks to the ostomy supply end / standard 90. Ostomy refill 2026-09-16 (90 days) ends 62 days ahead; grant to 2027-09-09 -> 60 days. Baseline 532.
  kit_room_rule [parameter]: kits shipped within 3 months -> allowance less the kit order quantity / within 12 months only -> allowance less a twelfth of the kit units / allowance. Kits 2026-07-17 -> 170. Baseline 392.
  above_allowance_route [parameter, multi-source: records, notices, orders]: over-limit record no more than 6 whole months old AND orders above the allowance -> the newest order's quantity for the standard supply days / no qualifying record AND a notice dated on or before the ship date -> the units on the newest notice / 0. Record 2026-03-02 is 7 months old; notice signed 2026-10-14 for 811 -> cap 811, extra min(811, 70) = 70. Baseline 292.
  increase_phase_in_rule [parameter]: raised order no more than 60 days old -> 1 block / 61 to 180 days -> 2 blocks / the standard blocks. Order 240 dated 2026-09-10 (34 days) vs 180 -> 1. Baseline 432.
  supply_start_anchor [method]: replacement shipped -> its ship date / POD more than 2 days after shipping -> the delivery date / the ship date. POD 2026-07-22 (5 days) -> 6 days left. Baseline 402.
  carry_rate_rule [parameter]: newest order dated after the previous refill AND raised -> order / 30 / kits shipped with the previous refill -> (refill + kit units) / supply days / refill units / supply days (0 when no supply days). -> 8 per day, unused 48. Baseline 374.
 Notice (5; 4 parameter, 1 method; result 811; all-baseline 120):
  notice_term_rule [parameter]: earlier order AND newest raises AND no more than 180 days old -> 12 blocks / earlier order AND newest asks no more AND no more than 180 days old -> 6 / one standard shipment (3). Raised, 34 days -> 12. Baseline 251.
  order_horizon_rule [method]: POD more than 2 days after shipping -> counted from delivery + supply days (or the signing date when that is past) / previous ship + supply days after the signing date -> from that date / from the signing date; whole blocks to the order's valid-through, never below zero. 2026-07-22 + 90 = 2026-10-20, 324 days -> 10. Notice blocks min(12, 10) = 10. Baseline 891.
  expected_denial_basis [parameter]: kits within 3 months -> order + kit qty - allowance / within 12 months -> order + a twelfth of kit units - allowance / order - allowance. -> 70. Baseline 506.
  shortfall_margin_rule [parameter]: customer-requested expedited refill within 12 months -> 10 / raised order no more than 60 days old -> 5 / 0. 2026-01-12 expedited refill -> 10. Baseline 711.
  delivery_cushion_rule [parameter]: order >= 240 -> 5 days / 180 to 239 -> 3 / 0. -> 11 units. Baseline 800.
 Hardship waiver (4; 3 parameter, 1 method; result 272.61; all-baseline 172.60):
  hardship_lookback_rule [method]: application no more than 120 days old -> time window, remittances within 6 calendar months / 121 to 365 days -> statement window, remittances of the latest remittance date / the named posting alone; the named posting is counted once, and only if it is a remittance. 177 days -> 2026-08-12 statement, 118.80 + 108.90 = 227.70. Baseline 67.68.
  open_amount_basis [parameter]: payments within 3 calendar months -> those payments set against the waived postings first / a prior adjustment on the named posting -> it / 0. 2026-08-21 120.00 + 2026-09-25 150.00 = 270.00 (2026-06-08 is 4 months back). Baseline 515.61.
  hardship_share_rule [parameter, multi-source, cross ostomy]: active ostomy AND the customer's latest ostomy hardship application approved within 12 months -> whole / an active ostomy program carrying a balance due (XMAX of balances over the customer's active ostomy programs > 0) -> 3/4 / 1/2. Ostomy balance 181.20; its 2026-07-09 application denied -> 0.75. Baseline 196.88.
  posting_age_rule [parameter]: named posting more than 180 days old -> +0.15 / 91 to 180 -> +0.10 / 0. 247 days -> +0.15. Baseline 227.17.
 Combination (the rules' generic combination sentence): waiver round((345.20 + 227.70 - 270.00) x min(1, 0.90), 2) = 272.61; notice (70 + 10) x 10 + int(70 x 5 / 30) = 811; refill min(240, 170) x 2 + min(811, (240 - 170) x min(1, 2)) - int(6 x 8) = 362 with 60 supply days. Multi-source factors 2 (above_allowance_route, hardship_share_rule); cross-difficulty factors 2 (sync_span_rule, hardship_share_rule, reading seeded Ostomy Supply Program rows by EXISTS/XMAX/XLATEST with the active-status filter; the first-active CFIELD balance read became a sum in round 3 and a maximum in round 4, exact for "an active program that carries a balance due above zero" even when another active program carries a credit; same value on this world).
4. Base-invariant card. Refill write (subject continence_refill_shipment): governing base policies continence_evt_refill_shipment, continence_agg_consolidated_supply, continence_evt_quantity_limits, continence_combo_indwelling_exclusion. Gates and authoritative evidence: program_active (status active); authorization_valid_on_ship_date (newest grant valid 2026-09-10..2027-09-09); units_within_authorization (authorized_units_remaining 3240 >= 362); refill_not_too_early [time: previous refill 2026-07-17 + 90 supply days = 2026-10-15, earliest 10 days before = 2026-10-05, inclusive; 2026-10-04 would be too early, 2026-10-05 and 2026-10-14 allowed]; coverage_recently_verified [time: last verified 2026-06-30, within 12 calendar months before the ship date, inclusive; holds through 2027-06-30]; bags_on_one_program (no bags on this line); items_match_line (A4351 on a straight-tip intermittent program); special_catheter_documented (no coude or closed-system item in this refill; the closed-system qualification of 2025-09-30 is on file for the kits); no_excluded_line_open (no indwelling program). Overwrites (each self-scoped "For a straight-tip intermittent catheter refill on the Original Medicare tier, and only for such a refill"): the base supply-days sentence (the span rule decides), the base units sentence (covered plus above-allowance less unused supply), and the base confirmation sentence - a genuine departure: the customer confirms continued use in the call, and the supply on hand is counted from the records by the unused-supply rule (6 days left) rather than from the customer's own count. Notice write: continence_liability_notice governs (policy_scope); its overwrite departs from the base signing sentence: the customer signs in the call through the step the agent hands over, or an authorized representative signs, and no Larkfield representative signs; the signing tool's capability description says the same since round 3. Waiver write: continence_evt_patient_account governs; three overwrites, each scoped to this hardship waiver alone with every other balance adjustment left under the base rule: (1) "only for postings named on a hardship application whose request status is approved" - the approval reaches the named posting and, through the look-back, the other remittances this policy names; (2) "each against the one posting it adjusts and never for more than that posting's unpaid remainder" - one adjustment against the named posting carries the whole waiver this policy computes, even above the named posting's unpaid remainder (round-4 wording, which no longer points at the look-back or the open-amount rule); (3) "a payment is applied to the oldest unpaid posting first" - for the waived amount only (round-6 wording: "the waived amount is counted by this policy's open-amount deduction, which sets the customer's recent payments against the waived amount first"), recent payments are set against it first. The approval stays a condition of the rule (initial_state.continence_requests.<hs>.request_status = approved). The small_balance_ceiling gate stays in force and is evidenced as not binding (it bounds small-balance write-offs; this is a hardship waiver, 272.61 <= balance 314.00).

5. Business-object card. Target: the straight-tip catheter (A4351) refill of the program. Correlation keys: program id, the newest A4351 grant, the previous A4351 refill (2026-07-17, 540 units, 90 days) and its POD (2026-07-22). Rows included: A4351 orders (180 -> 240), A4353 kit orders and refills (room, denial basis, rate), over-limit records (newest 2026-03-02), the notice signed today. Excluded: kit refills as "previous refill" (item filter), the 2026-09-10 follow-up record (purpose continued_need_followup), the expired 2025-10-10 grant. Waiver object: the approved application names the 2026-02-09 straight-tip remittance (345.20); the statement window adds the two 2026-08-12 remittances (118.80, 108.90); no adjustment exists before the call; payments are not linked to postings, so the open-amount rule sets the last 3 months' payments against the waived set.

6. Initial-state rows (closure 77 = seed 77). customers/coverages: identity and the Part B coverage (last verified 2026-06-30). continence_programs (1): tier, status, tip, units 3240 (2160+360+2880+360 credited - 4x540 - 4x90), balance 314.00 (1137.20 + 24.50 - 847.70). continence_orders (13): two A4351 orders, two A4353 orders, four grants, closed-system qualification, two over-limit records, one follow-up record. continence_shipments (16): four A4351 + four A4353 refills (2025-10-14, 2026-01-12 expedited, 2026-04-13, 2026-07-17) with eight PODs. continence_billing (22): eight original claims, eight Medicare remittances (20% coinsurance; the first 2026 straight-tip claim also carries the Part B deductible: 594.00 - 248.80 = 345.20), the 24.50 expedited charge, five payments. continence_requests (1): the approved hardship application. Ostomy (read-only, legal ostomy states): an active Ostomy Original Medicare colostomy two-piece program, its two orders and grants, refills of 2026-06-18 and 2026-09-16 (A4414 60 units, A4423 180 units, 90 days) with PODs, claims and remittances (20%), a 181.20 payment of the June responsibility, balance 181.20 = the September responsibility, and a denied hardship application. Removing the ostomy program's active status drops the sync tier (refill 532) and the share tier (waiver 196.88); removing the kit refills drops the room and denial-basis tiers; removing the 2026-07-22 POD moves the supply start (refill 402); removing the approved application removes the waiver (0). Automatic clauses checked: no hold (status active), every refill has its claim, no credit balance (41.39 after the waiver), no refund or small-balance write-off owed (OM write-off threshold 0.00), no lost package; the ostomy program owes nothing.

7. Persona design. Thaddeus Wrenfield (surname unique in this difficulty and the blueprint). Plain, slightly gruff retired furniture maker; volunteers only the goal (next shipment at the new amount, standard shipping, no kits). Given only when asked: name and phone, date of birth, continued use and about six days on hand (consistent with the six days the records show; the count is not what fixes the units), address on file, no kits. Passive: signs the notice for the units the agent states once it is explained and handed over; accepts any account change; closes when told the shipment is on its way. He never names notices, waivers or balances first.

8. Reachability walk. find_customers(name, phone) -> verify(DOB, phone) -> programs, coverages -> billing (no adjustment on the named posting) -> requests (approved application unapplied) -> ostomy programs/requests/billing (share evidence) -> unlock + call waiver 272.61 -> orders (orders, records, grants) -> shipments (refills, PODs, kits, expedited) -> explain the notice, unlock_user + customer signs 811 -> ostomy orders/shipments (sync evidence) -> unlock + call refill 362 / 60 days. One frozen_time 2026-10-14 10:20:00 EDT; no step waits on delivery, payment clearing or payer review.

9. Careless paths. Ships 240 x 3 = 720 or 200 x 3 = 600; counts the aged-out March record; anchors the previous supply at the ship date (402); values the unused days at 6 per day (374); ignores the ostomy sync (532) or the kit room (392); signs a one-shipment notice (251) or counts the horizon from today (891); forgets the kits in the expected denial (506); posts the waiver on the named posting only (67.68) or ignores the recent payments (515.61); takes the half share (196.88) or skips the age addition (227.17); ships before the waiver adjustment stands (the refill's sentence waits on it).

10. Factor-independence table (deps.py, transitive reads; reads-other-factor = none for all): refill - sync_span_rule plain {auth_days, std_days}, kit_room_rule {allowance, kit_qty}, above_allowance_route {allowance, kit_qty, notice_date_on_file, notice_units_on_file, order_qty, record_visit, std_blocks}, increase_phase_in_rule {newest_order_date, order_qty, prev_order_qty, std_blocks}, supply_start_anchor {prev_id, prev_ship}, carry_rate_rule {newest_order_date, order_qty, prev_days, prev_order_qty, prev_ship, prev_units}; notice - notice_term_rule {newest_order_date, order_qty, prev_order_qty, std_blocks}, order_horizon_rule {order_through, prev_days, prev_id, prev_ship}, expected_denial_basis {allowance, kit_qty, order_qty}, shortfall_margin_rule {newest_order_date, order_qty, prev_order_qty}, delivery_cushion_rule {order_qty}; waiver - hardship_lookback_rule {app_date, named_amt, named_date, named_type}, open_amount_basis {named_id}, hardship_share_rule {}, posting_age_rule {named_date}. All INDEPENDENT; shared selections are plain bindings stated once in each rule's "Records read" paragraph, and result assembles the amount.

11. Pairwise method-tier table (pair: distinguishing input -> values). sync_span_rule: A/B: grant valid through 2026-11-20 -> 192 vs 362; A/C: the same grant with the ostomy program closed -> 192 vs 532 (ostomy closed, grant to 2027-09-09); B/C: ostomy program active vs closed -> 362 vs 532. supply_start_anchor: A/B: a replacement shipped 2026-07-25 -> 338 vs 362; A/C: replacement vs a POD 1 day after shipping -> 338 vs 402; B/C: POD 2026-07-22 vs 2026-07-18 -> 362 vs 402. order_horizon_rule: A/B: order valid through 2027-09-14 with POD 2026-07-22 (A, 329 days, 10 blocks) vs POD 2026-07-18 (B, 334 days, 11 blocks) -> 811 vs 891; A/C: gold vs the July refill shipped 2026-07-10 with POD 2026-07-11 (C, 330 days, 11 blocks) -> 811 vs 891; B/C: POD 2026-07-18 (B, 10 blocks) vs shipped 2026-07-10 (C) -> 811 vs 891. hardship_lookback_rule: A/B: application 2026-06-16 (120 days) vs 2026-04-20 -> 477.54 vs 272.61; A/C: 2026-06-16 vs 2025-10-13 (366 days) -> 477.54 vs 67.68; B/C: 2025-10-14 (365 days, B) vs 2025-10-13 -> 272.61 vs 67.68.

12. Probe table (probe_t0.py on scratch copies; waiver, notice, refill; base 272.61, 811, 362; each policy is recomputed on the world at its own gold step). First-match and CFIELD reads: a newer refill of another item (A4352) -> unchanged (item filter); a replacement for the April refill -> unchanged (keyed to the previous refill); a replacement for the July refill -> refill 338; the follow-up record dated today -> unchanged (purpose filter); an over-limit record within 6 months -> unchanged (first tier caps at 720, still above 70); a closed ostomy program with a 500.00 balance alongside -> unchanged (active filter); a second active ostomy program with balance 0.00 listed first -> unchanged, and with the real program's balance at 0.00 and a second active program carrying 50.00 listed first -> unchanged 272.61 (any active program with a balance counts; the only program at 0.00 alone -> 196.88); a second active program carrying a 300.00 credit beside the 181.20 balance -> unchanged 272.61 (round 4: a maximum, not a sum); two active programs at 0.00 and a 20.00 credit -> 196.88; a newer denied continence hardship application -> unchanged (approved filter); the named posting being the expedited fee (not a remittance) -> not subtracted from the window, waived amount below zero -> 0.00. Absent records: no previous straight-tip refill -> no earlier order and no unused supply: notice 251, refill 480; no POD -> refill 402; no approved application -> waiver 0; no payments within 3 months -> 515.61; no ostomy requests -> unchanged; ostomy application approved -> 302.90. None edges: ostomy refill supply days None -> no ostomy supply end, standard span, refill 532 (guard added this round); previous refill supply days None -> 0 supply days, no unused supply, refill 410, notice 891; order valid-through None -> zero horizon, notice 11 (cushion only). Zero division: no previous supply days with a non-raising order -> rate 0 (guard added to the binding and the baseline), refill 360. Date edges: order dated 180 days before signing -> 12-block term, notice 811 (refill 438, phase-in second tier); 181 days -> standard term, 251; application at 120 days -> time window 477.54, at 365 days -> statement window, at 366 -> named posting alone; the delivery-based horizon start is never before the signing date (clamp added this round). Quantifier sweep (round 3): the route's "no over-limit record qualifies" and "a notice dated on or before the ship date is on file" are read through the newest record and the newest notice; because the refill ships on the handling date, a record or notice is never dated after it, so the newest one decides the existential exactly (a record within 6 whole months exists iff the newest is; a notice on or before today exists iff the newest is); the hardship look-back, deduction and share tests are counts and sums over windows or exact filters. Rounding: refill and notice round down to whole units; waiver 302.90 x 0.90 = 272.61 exactly, no half-cent tie.

13. Recomputation and gates. sens.py at handling time: waiver 272.61 (step 10), notice 811 (step 14, after the waiver), refill 362 with 60 supply days (step 18, after both). Per-task gates on task 0: EXTENDED OK, SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, REPLAY OK.

14. Draft recomputation from the visible context. The refill rule's two prerequisite sentences point at the approved application's unapplied waiver and the missing signed notice; the hardship rule gives (345.20 + 227.70 - 270.00) x (0.75 + 0.15) = 272.61; the notice rule gives (70 + 10) x 10 + 11 = 811; the refill rule gives 170 x 2 + min(811, 70) - 6 x 8 = 362 with 60 supply days. No second reading was found: the look-back and age tiers fall on clean day counts (177 and 247), the record is 7 whole months old, and the sync window (62 days) sits inside 30 to 89.

Revision log. R1: refill room factor was decorative while the notice covered all excess -> added the increase phase-in. R2: a coverage horizon factor could not be computed -> replaced by a delivery-based count in the notice. R3: the waiver could exceed the balance -> application moved to 2026-04-20 and recent payments added. R4: caller-statement gates -> declared scoped overwrites. R5: closure missed 13 ostomy rows -> added ostomy reads. R6: absent-record guards and the active-status filter on ostomy reads. Rework round 2: factor bindings that read other factors' values were rebuilt so every shared selection is a plain binding (deps.py INDEPENDENT); the notice term became a raised/renewed/standard parameter and the term-start factor became the order-horizon method; the look-back became a time/statement/none window method counting the named posting once, only if it is a remittance; the route became a record/notice parameter matching the edge sentence; the edge-2 sentence now names the newest approved application exactly as the rule reads it; the confirmation and signing overwrites now state genuine departures; the payment-order departure is declared (overwrite 3); the small-balance overwrite and the return-credit carve-out in the hardship tails were removed (both gates stay under base); probe guards (ostomy supply days, rate baseline, horizon clamp) were added; values unchanged. Rework round 3: the hardship share's balance test sums the balances of every active ostomy program (exact for "an active program that carries a balance due"), and its approval test names the customer's latest ostomy hardship application; the signing tool's docstring admits the authorized representative; this task's world and values are unchanged (272.61, 811, 362).

Rework round 4 (KB audit, source-side). F-5: the hardship share's balance test reads the largest balance due over the customer's active ostomy programs (XMAX), exact for "an active Ostomy Supply Program that carries a balance due above zero"; probes above. E-2 (source side): overwrite 2's replaced_by now reads "carries the whole waiver this policy computes, even where that is more than the named posting's unpaid remainder", so the computation document no longer points at the look-back or the open-amount rule. Baselines: the standard-method paragraphs of the refill, notice and waiver no longer name factor defaults ("No above-allowance units ship", "adds no margin and no cushion", "with no look-back postings", "no deduction is made", "with no addition"); each now states the factor-free figure (refill: covered units times blocks less the unused supply, 594; notice: expected-denial quantity times the notice blocks, 120; waiver: one half of the named posting, 172.60), and the general formulas moved to Assembly paragraphs. Closure: the waiver edge's why_false, flips and edge_load_bearing now speak only of the adjustment the sentence waits on, not of the past-due amount. World and values unchanged (272.61, 811, 362).

Rework round 5 (XF class: S-1, S-2). The refill, notice and waiver rules were rewritten so that each Standard method paragraph defines its plain quantities in record terms and yields a definite figure (refill 594, notice 120, waiver 172.60), a single generic combination sentence states how adjustments apply (replacements of a standard quantity first and the quantities resting on it counted again, then additions, each within its own limit), and each factor paragraph states how it changes a standard quantity, reading only records and standard quantities: the span replaces the supply days; the kit room replaces the covered limit; the route adds the order's excess for the refill (a plain quantity defined once in the standard method) within its own cap; the phase-in replaces the blocks for which that excess counts; the supply start replaces the previous supply's start; the rate replaces the daily rate; the notice term replaces the term blocks; the horizon is counted from another start; the expected-denial basis replaces the expected-denial quantity; the margin and the cushion add units; the look-back adds remittance postings to the waived amount, the deduction takes payments from it, the hardship share replaces the waiver share and the posting age adds to it (S-2: it no longer reads the hardship share's quantity), the share never more than the whole. Overwrite 2 of the refill now reads 'the units are those this policy states'. Compute changes: covered_per30 is a new plain binding; values unchanged (272.61, 811, 362). XF mechanical check (xfcheck.py): baseline.rule, the result quote and every non-factor compute_basis quote name no factor quantity or trigger (refill, notice, waiver: none); no factor binding reads another factor's binding transitively (refill, notice, waiver: none).

Rework round 6 (R5-1, O19, O20). R5-1: the hardship compute_basis quote for ostomy_active now quotes the rule fragment "When the customer also holds an Ostomy Supply Program in active status"; a scratch check (qcheck.py) confirmed every compute_basis quote of all six policies (112 quotes), every replaced_by and every baseline.rule is verbatim in its rule (0 misses). O19: overwrite 3 of the hardship policy and its rule sentence now read "the waived amount is counted by this policy's open-amount deduction, which sets the customer's recent payments against the waived amount first". O20: the refill -> notice edge effect, this closure's why_false and flips_to_true_by, and this dossier no longer use "route cap", "increase blocks" or "straight-tip room". Values and tools unchanged.
user_scenario:
You are Thaddeus Wrenfield, 72, a retired furniture maker who lives in Hillsborough, North Carolina. A fall from a ladder in 2019 left you paraplegic. You catheterize several times a day with straight-tip catheters, keep a few closed-system kits for trips, and have a colostomy; Larkfield Medical Supply sends you both your catheters and your ostomy supplies. You talk slowly and plainly, a little gruff, and you like to get to the point.

You are calling because your urologist raised you to eight catheters a day at your visit last month and you are getting near the end of your current supply.
